newsitem.title: FRANCE: Moslem rebels kill 100 civilians in Algeria - paper.
newsitem.headline: Moslem rebels kill 100 civilians in Algeria - paper.

text.p: Moslem rebels killed more than 100 civilians in a series of massacres in Algeria overnight on Sunday-Monday, the Algerian newspaper Le Matin said on Tuesday.
Other Algerian newspapers put the death toll in the attacks at up to 75, with the rebels dragging off young girls with them as they fled.

The killings bring to at least 250 the toll among civilians in the past 10 days. The Sunday slaughter coincided with a vow by President Liamine Zeroual that the authorities would implacably pursue the rebels whose violence, he said, had "cruelly plunged the Algerian family into mourning".
Le Matin said 26 people were killed in Amroussa village in Bouinan district, Blida province, some 50 km (30 miles) south of the capital Algiers in an attack just before midnight on Sunday.
In another series of attacks in the province of Ain Defla, some 110 km (70 miles) southwest of Algiers, a total of 76 civilians were killed in four villages.
Eight more people were killed and seven wounded at a fake road block in Hammam Melouane, the newspaper said.
